extractor_notes: Proposed classes 1, 2, 4, 6(a), and 6(b) appear in the Final Rule's section C 'Classes Considered but Not Recommended' (PDF pp. 8-9). Class 5 was partially denied: a narrow exemption for retail-level commercial food preparation equipment was granted, but the broader proposed class covering all software-enabled commercial and industrial equipment was declined (PDF p. 7). Class 6(a) was partially denied: the Register declined to remove the single-user limitation as proposed, but adopted clarifying language; she rejected the proposed expansion's substantive effect, so it is captured here as a denial. Note that the 2021 (b)(21) Video Games accessibility input-methods exemption was not renewed because no petition was filed (PDF p. 6, footnote 21 context) -- per task instructions, this is tracked separately in analysis/lineages.json and is not listed here. PDF pages cited refer to [PAGE N] markers in the .txt extraction.

denials.reason_quote: The Office received no comments in support of the proposal, no requests from OTW or other parties to participate in the public hearings, and no other evidence in support of the proposal. ... The Register does not recommend the expansion proposed as Class 1, which does not include substantive changes.

denials.topic_label: Audiovisual Works -- Online Learning (MOOC expansion to for-profit/unaccredited)
denials.reason_quote: The Register finds that the record lacks support to expand the existing exemption to for-profit and/or unaccredited educational entities. She therefore does not recommend adopting the proposed exemption.

denials.topic_label: Computer Programs -- Generative AI Trustworthiness Research
denials.reason_quote: The Register recommends denying the proposed exemption. ... She finds, however, that the adverse effects identified by proponents arise from third-party control of online platforms rather than the operation of section 1201, so that an exemption would not ameliorate their concerns.

denials.topic_label: Computer Programs -- Repair of Commercial/Industrial Equipment (beyond food preparation)
denials.reason_quote: However, she declines to recommend an exemption for a broader class of software-enabled commercial and industrial devices in the absence of a sufficient showing of adverse effects on the record presented in this rulemaking.

The Register concludes that proponents did not show that removing the single-user limitation for preserved computer programs or permitting off-premises access to video games are likely to be noninfringing.

denials.topic_label: Video Games -- Preservation (remove premises limitation for off-site access)
denials.reason_quote: She also notes the greater risk of market harm with removing the video game exemption's premises limitation, given the market for legacy video games.
